content.text:
This confirms it: the same commit that added this switch statement also defined the correctly-named enum constants (`ReservationPriorityGroup`, `ReservationPriorityCourse`, `ReservationPriorityCurriculum`, etc.), but the switch statement itself mistakenly used `...Individual` for all four cases (Individual, Group, Curriculum, Course) — a copy-paste error where the same block was duplicated without updating the property names.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 18f154d85110c36f6eb403d0a33703db4cfe8175

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I ran `git log --follow -p` on `XReservation.java` to trace the full history of the switch statement that the fix commit modifies. This showed the switch statement (with `case Group/Curriculum/Course`) did not always exist — it was introduced in commit `18f154d8` (2014-12-05), and has remained textually unchanged (for these specific lines) from that point all the way until the fix commit `6eb8807d` (2016-02-22).

**(2) Specific change:** In `18f154d8`, the author added a new `switch (type)` block in the `XReservation` constructor to initialize priority/overlap/limit/mustBeUsed settings per reservation type. However, they copy-pasted the `case Individual:` body into `case Group:`, `case Curriculum:`, and `case Course:` without updating the `ApplicationProperty` references — all four cases call `...Individual` getters instead of their respective `...Group`, `...Curriculum`, `...Course` getters.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** The same commit (`18f154d8`) also adds the `ApplicationProperty.java` enum entries `ReservationPriorityGroup`, `ReservationPriorityCourse`, `ReservationPriorityCurriculum` (and their `MustBeUsed`/`CanOverLimit`/`AllowOverlap` counterparts) — proving these correct properties existed and were available for use at the time but were simply never wired into the switch statement due to the copy-paste. No other commit in the file's history touches these specific lines between `18f154d8` and the fix `6eb8807d`, confirming the bug was present continuously since its introduction.

I'm highly confident in this attribution — the evidence (unused-but-defined properties in the same commit, plus an unbroken `git log -p` history showing no intermediate edits to these lines) is direct and unambiguous.
